name: GreekBarBench
description: We introduce GreekBarBench, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs on legal questions across five different legal areas from the Greek Bar exams, requiring citations to statutory articles and case facts. To tackle the challenges of free-text evaluation, we propose a three-dimensional scoring system combined with an LLM-as-a-judge approach. We also develop a meta-evaluation benchmark to assess the correlation between LLM-judges and human expert evaluations, revealing that simple, span-based rubrics improve their alignment. Our systematic evaluation of 13 proprietary and open-weight LLMs shows that even though the best models outperform average expert scores, they fall short of the 95th percentile of experts.
evaluation_method: human_eval (rubric-based), supplemented by an LLM-as-judge automated scoring pipeline
general_score_metric: composite rubric score (three-dimensional: legal correctness, citation/factual grounding, application to facts)
notes: High risk of training-data contamination for proprietary LLMs (bar/exam content); evaluation is complex and partly subjective despite rubrication; requires citation grounding and long-form reasoning — not directly comparable to simple QA benchmarks.
